title: More partitions than errors
prompt: This program spreads the `error_events` table and compares the result with the original. What does it print? Type each line on its own line.
program:
spread = error_events.repartition(6)
print(spread.columns == error_events.columns)
print(len(spread.columns), spread.count())
print(spread.rdd.getNumPartitions() - spread.count(), "partitions at least are empty")
hints: `repartition` moves rows between partitions. Does it touch the columns?
Count the columns and the rows of `error_events`.
With more partitions than rows, some partitions must be empty: at least partitions minus rows.
explanation: `repartition` keeps the same columns in the same order, so the lists are equal (`True`). `error_events` has 8 columns and 4 rows, and spreading 4 rows over 6 partitions leaves at least 2 of them empty.
